title: Working on 7 game projects with ChatGPT and Codex, looking to connect with other AI game developers
author: Junior_Muffin5931
selftext: Hey everyone! I'm 31 and from Pennsylvania. I've been using ChatGPT and Codex to work on seven gaming projects, and I'm hoping to meet some people with similar interests, exchange ideas and hopefully make a few friends. My projects include ADHD Pixel Dungeon, an expanded roguelike; Monster Civilization, a civilization simulator starting with five rats; Lastlight Company, a long-term incremental RPG; President of the Office, a satirical presidential management game; Tenths, a motorsport management simulator; and Android ports of Trimps and Increlution. The two ports are currently for personal use while I sort out the necessary authorization for public distribution. All the ideas, mechanics and design decisions come from me, while AI handles much of the actual programming and implementation. I spend a ridiculous amount of time designing systems, testing builds, finding bugs and correcting AI mistakes. I've already invested hundreds of hours into these projects, and some have working Android builds. I'm not a traditional programmer, but I've found a way to bring ideas to life that I could never realistically implement entirely on my own. I'd love to connect with other people doing something similar, hear about what you're building and maybe even make some gaming friends along the way!

I do similar. But, I keep one game as my priority long term. Recently my son asked me for a game, and I took a break from my main game to whip something up for him, and I’ll have Claude do it with his instructions - and yes, I have him write up instructions for me to submit - while I’m thinking about a different direction. I’ll get other ideas for games and write them down, too. 

One of the problems is that you or I cannot keep it all straight in our heads. Design docs are required for everything, and you’ll need to keep really good organization of those docs to prevent drift and slop.

replies.author: Junior_Muffin5931
replies.body: Hey, I'd definitely be interested in connecting! I'm currently working on seven game projects with AI-assisted development, and I've been looking into building reusable tools to make the development process easier. I recently had Codex audit eight of my GitHub repositories, and it identified quite a bit of existing infrastructure I could reuse. I'm planning a shared toolkit with five tools: a universal bug investigator, automated game tester, numerical balance auditor, Android build verifier, and a design authorization system that prevents AI agents from implementing features without my approval. Most of the foundations already exist across my projects, but they still need to be consolidated into something reusable. I'd love to hear what tools you've built and how you approach your daily prototyping!

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body: Just start by consolidating the skills into reusable skills and then you can build plug-ins. That’s what I do for everything whether it be software development game development or AI research.
